subject: Engage.ai demo — recommended engines, risk notes & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Moroz <sylvia@engage.ai>, Roberto Vega <r.vega@nova-olympus.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Engage.ai demo — recommended engines, risk notes & next steps

Hi Sylvia / Roberto — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and our recommended path so we keep the evaluation focused: 

High-level recommendation (shortlist):
- Engine-A-q8a (8-bit quantized, tuned KV cache) — best cost profile, ~2–2.5x cheaper than fp16 for your typical 512-token responses; p95 latency ~170–220ms in our hosted region. Strong for short-answer contact resolution.
- Engine-B-fp16 (fp16, faster kernels) — higher quality on multi-turn clarification (lower omission/hallucination), p95 latency ~120–160ms, cost ~1.8x Engine-A.
- Engine-C-fused (smaller parameter variant) — fallback for burst/high-concurrency; latency and cost are best but expect lower accuracy on long-form extraction.

Tradeoffs to flag:
- Cost vs quality: Engine-A compresses cost but shows ~6% higher hallucination on our internal NER/regression prompts vs Engine-B.
- Latency SLOs: If you need p95 < 150ms consistently, Engine-B or reserved Dedicated capacity will be necessary. Engine-A meets SLOs only with pinned capacity or aggressive batching guardrails.
- Regression risk: prompt drift and prompt-engine mismatch are the leading causes we saw in the demo transcripts. We recommend a small regression harness (attached) that runs the core prompt set against each engine nightly during the pilot.

Attachments included for your review: engage_benchmarks_v1.csv (benchmark traces), prompt_set_contact_resolution_v2.json (30 canonical prompts), latency_cost_estimates.xlsx, eval-harness-notes.pdf. Links also in the footer.

Suggested next steps (proposal):
1) 2-week focused eval sprint: Redwood will run Engine-A and Engine-B on your canonical prompt set plus 25 proprietary edge cases you provide.
2) Instrumented metrics: hallucination rate (entity hallucinations per 1k tokens), semantic F1 for extraction, p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens.
3) Set up a shared dashboard and weekly 30-min sync (Mon mornings) for the sprint.
4) Decision point: choose engine for pilot or request Dedicated trial (if latency SLOs require it).

Can you confirm: 1) you’re okay with the two-week sprint scope, and 2) who on your side will upload the 25 edge-case prompts to the Drive folder linked below?

Thanks — I’ll schedule the first sync once you confirm.

—
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Engage.ai demo — recommended engines, risk notes & next steps

Thanks Dylan — useful summary. A few clarifying Qs before we lock the sprint: 

- Hallucination definition: can you confirm the exact criteria you used to get that ~6% delta? We track two flavors — (A) hallucinated entities (invented phone numbers/emails) and (B) confabbed relationships (wrong company ties). Which did you measure?
- Edge-case upload: I’ll have engineering drop the 25 cases in the Drive by EOD Friday (point person: me).
- Data residency: we prefer evaluation to run in us-east region only. Is that straightforward?
- Procurement: our procurement team may request an NDA addendum for the pilot — can your legal team fast-track a one-page SOW? Our timeline is tight (decision by 6/20).

Also, would you add a simple scoring rubric we can use during the sprint so engineering and product align on pass/fail for the Decision Point? A single-sheet with metrics + thresholds would be ideal.

On the hallucination note — we have a few multi-turn threads in the demo where the model guessed contact titles incorrectly. If Engine-B reduces those failures by half vs Engine-A, that might be enough for us to accept the cost delta.

Best,
Sylvia
Head of Product, Engage.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Moroz <sylvia@engage.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-03T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Engage.ai demo — recommended engines, risk notes & next steps

Sylvia — quick technical answers and a proposed rubric. Quoting Dylan below for context:

> - Hallucination definition: can you confirm the exact criteria you used to get that ~6% delta?

We used (A) hallucinated entities count per 1k tokens as the primary metric for the benchmark CSV. That is: any extracted entity in the model output not present in the ground truth set (false positive). (B) confabbed relationships were tracked as a secondary signal (semantic F1). Engine-A had ~6% higher false-positive entity rate on our 30-prompt canonical set; the semantic F1 gap vs Engine-B was ~3.5 points.

Proposed one-page scoring rubric (summary):
- Hallucination (entity FP per 1k tokens): pass <= 1.2, warn 1.2–2.0, fail > 2.0
- Semantic F1 (extraction tasks): pass >= 86, warn 78–86, fail < 78
- Latency p95 (us-east): pass <= 200ms, warn 200–300ms, fail > 300ms
- Cost per 1k tokens (pilot volumes): pass <= $1.20, warn $1.20–$1.80, fail > $1.80

Notes on data residency: we can run the entire eval in us-east; please confirm the region in the Drive upload metadata. Dedicated trial (if chosen) would be in us-east as well.

Operational recommendations to reduce regression risk:
- Prefix caching: seed the KV cache with typical conversation prefixes for Engage flows to reduce early-turn hallucinations.
- Temperature clamping: run deterministic temp <= 0.4 for extraction prompts.
- Output filters: implement a lightweight pattern filter for phone/email formats to post-process outputs and reduce entity hallucinations.
- Nightly regression harness: run canonical prompts on both engines on a small fleet, diff the outputs, and flag deviations >5% in entity FP as automatic alerts.

I attached a short eval-harness-notes.pdf and left an example harness script in the Drive link. I can spin up a temporary workspace for you if you want us to run the first nightly job.

—
Ben Carter
Principal Product Engineer, Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks Sylvia and Ben. Quick mutual action items to lock the sprint and procurement cadence: 

1) Sylvia: upload the 25 edge-case prompts to the Drive folder and mark region = us-east in the file metadata (target: 2028-06-07 EOD).
2) Redwood (Ben + Dylan): we will run the 2-week sprint starting 2028-06-10 if datasets are in place. We’ll run Engine-A-q8a and Engine-B-fp16 nightly, populate the rubric sheet, and share a dashboard by day 3.
3) Procurement/legal: Marissa — can you start the one-page SOW and NDA addendum? We need procurement sign-off window (requested decision 2028-06-20).
4) Sync: Proposed kickoff + scoreboard walkthrough on 2028-06-11 at 10am PT. I’ll send a calendar invite once Sylvia confirms dataset upload.

If Engine-B proves materially better on semantic F1 and halves the entity FP rate vs Engine-A, we will present the Dedicated recommendation and a cost supplement for predictable latency. Otherwise, default to Engine-A for cost efficiency and a few extra post-processing filters.

Thanks — looking forward to the sprint.

Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
